item.title: Bengals safety Bryan Cook injured vs Ravens in NFL Week 7
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals safety Bryan Cook was injured during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 7 game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Cook was in on a sack of Ravens quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley. Medical personnel look at Cook's lower body, before Cook got up and walked slowly off the field. Fellow safety Kyle Dugger left the game and was ruled out earlier in the second half. Cook hurt his ankle during the first quarter of the team's NFL Week 3 loss in Pittsburgh. Cook missed two games because of the injury. Cook, a former Mount Healthy High School standout and Cincinnati Bearcats defensive back, was on the sideline after having his ankle taped during the Steelers' second scoring drive of the game. Cook returned to the game early in the second quarter. Cook agreed to terms March 9 on a reported three-year deal worth $40.25 million. "My family's been talking about this for a long time," Cook said March 12. "Being able to come back home and … be closer to our family. I'm just excited for the opportunity, excited for the new chapter in my life." Cook was at Kansas City's T-Mobile Center to watch the ninth-seeded Bearcats ' men's basketball team defeat No. 16 seed Utah in the Big 12 tournament. Cook starred at UC from 2019 to 2021 before becoming a second-round pick of the Chiefs in 2022. The incident began in the offense’s meeting room when Simmons sat with his feet elevated. Reid directed him to place his feet on the floor. item.title: Amorim: ‘Milan players unavailable, Bournemouth were not better than us’
item.description: Amorim: ‘Milan players unavailable, Bournemouth were not better than us’ Ruben Amorim explains his Milan choices against Udinese, reveals he spoke to Mike Maignan about that red card. ‘Bournemouth weren’t better than us, they were more competitive.’ It kicks off at the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine at 19.45 GMT (20.45 CET). You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from today’s Serie A games on the Liveblog. The Rossoneri were shaken by Thursday’s 3-0 Europa League defeat at Bournemouth , a game that barely got started before the Mike Maignan red card ruined their plans. On top of that, Adrien Rabiot, Mario Gila and Diego Moreira sustained injuries, with Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano already out of action. Amorim forced to reshuffle Milan pack BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 22: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AFC Bournemouth and AC Milan at Bournemouth Stadium on October 22, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) “They cannot play, it’s just not possible. We need to manage the players, and there are players here today too where we need to manage their minutes,” Amorim told DAZN Italia when asked if some of those were precautionary decisions ahead of the midweek round. “With this schedule, it’s impossible to use everyone at the same time. Because we need to try to win every game, we need to balance everything, and they are not available for today.” Fikayo Tomori and Sankhoun Diawara get their first Serie A starts of the season in a revamped defence, while there are suggestions this might be a 4-4-2 formation. SALZBURG, AUSTRIA – OCTOBER 15: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, interacts with his players warming up during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Salzburg and AC Milan at Stadion Salzburg on October 15, 2026 in Salzburg, Austria. (Photo by Jasmin Walter/Getty Images) “We know that Udinese have five players at the back, so we try to play in a different way,” noted Amorim. “What matters is the rotation, I try to choose the players that are available physically, and then look at their characteristics. If I had all the players then I might play a different way, but today my feeling is this is the best starting XI for the game. It won’t be the line-up to finish, but it’s the best to start.” Maignan was sent off for a shove on Bournemouth player Tyler Adams as a corner was coming in, a naïve error that proved very costly indeed. Has Amorim spoken to Maignan about that incident? “The players are not boys, they are men. Maignan understood right away he cannot do that, we cannot put ourselves in that position,” replied the coach. item.title: Manchester United board hold crisis talks over Carrick’s future and Howe approach
item.description: Job in balance after 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth Howe is director of football Jason Wilcox’s top candidate Manchester United’s hierarchy are in crisis talks over whether or not to sack Michael Carrick as manager after he oversaw another torrid defeat , to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday, that appeared to leave his job in the balance. Carrick was defiant after the 3-0 humbling, insisting he was not expecting to be removed from his post, but the United executive were actively considering doing so, the Guardian understands. Eddie Howe remains the preferred candidate of Jason Wilcox, United’s director of football, should there be a change in the dugout, with the former Newcastle manager’s extensive Premier League experience placing him ahead of other potential targets. Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, given Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for the Spaniard. Continue reading...

item.title: Sammy Smith Delivers an Amazing Weekend With Historic Talladega Sweep
item.description: Photo by: Joe Puetz Smith Wins in Both the Truck and O’Reilly Series Sammy Smith put together one of the most impressive weekends of his racing career at Talladega Superspeedway, sweeping the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series and O’Reilly Auto Parts Series races with two dramatic victories. Smith started the weekend with a major announcement, confirming he will compete full-time in the Truck Series with TRICON Garage in 2027. He then backed up that news by delivering on the track, winning Friday’s Love’s RV Stop 225 before returning Saturday to capture The Progress Group 250 with JR Motorsports. The double victory made Smith the first non Cup Series driver since Greg Biffle in 2001 to win both a Truck Series race and an O’Reilly Series race at the same track during the same weekend. Smith Shows His Talent at Talladega Friday’s Truck Series victory was a significant moment for Smith, who captured his first career win in the series. He made the most of an overtime opportunity, edging Tyler Ankrum by just 0.091 seconds in a thrilling finish. Smith had little time to celebrate, however, with another race waiting on Saturday. Driving the No. 8 Chevrolet for JR Motorsports, Smith qualified 11th for the O’Reilly Series event and spent much of the afternoon working through the field. Carson Kvapil controlled much of the race, leading 67 of the 94 laps, while Smith stayed within striking distance. When the race reached its final lap, Smith made his move. With help from teammate Justin Allgaier and a push from championship contender Jesse Love, Smith surged past Kvapil and reached the finish line first by just 0.084 seconds. The victory ended Smith’s 53 race winless streak in the O’Reilly Series and marked his fourth career win in the division. His move to TRICON Garage in 2027 gives him an opportunity to build on the momentum generated by his Talladega success. Although Smith is no longer competing for the O’Reilly Series championship this season, his back-to-back victories demonstrated his ability to perform under pressure and capitalize on opportunities. For JR Motorsports, the win also delivered another memorable moment in a successful season. Smith arrived at Talladega with something to prove and left with two trophies. Winning twice in two different NASCAR national series over one weekend is an extraordinary accomplishment, and his performance could be a major confidence boost heading into the final races of the year. After a weekend like this, Sammy Smith has given racing fans plenty of reasons to be excited about what comes next.

item.title: ‘That ain’t it’: Former NFL running back reacts to ‘wild’ call against Cam Skattebo
item.description: Oct 18, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) leaves the field after a game against the New Orleans Saints at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images Cam Skattebo is having a rough couple of weeks on the field. A critical fumble two weeks ago led to being benched last week, and today, Skattebo’s return to the starting lineup was dimmed by a controversial penalty early on. On the New York Giants’ second drive of the game against the Houston Texans, Skattebo gained seven yards on first down, but was flagged for unnecessary roughness because the official said he lowered his head and initiated contact with Huston Texans safety M.J. Stewart. Holy Cam Skattebo! https://t.co/8p0gsxaukg — ΛWTHΞИƬIK (@awthentik) October 25, 2026 Skattebo was livid at the call, and so was Giants head coach John Harbaugh. The ref’s decision also drew criticism on social media, including from one former NFL running back. ‘That ain’t it’ Jacob Hester, who starred at LSU before suiting up for the San Diego Chargers (2008-11) and Denver Broncos (2012), was a physical, bruising runner unafraid of contact during his playing days. Now a SiriusXM NFL radio host, Hester was not feeling the flag on Skattebo. “Cam Skattebo getting called for unnecessary roughness as the BALL CARRIER is wild,” he tweeted . “You’ve got 11 dudes coming downhill with bad intentions trying to put you on the ground. But when you truck somebody in the hole, it’s a penalty? Nah, that ain’t it.” In case you thought Hester was being biased towards a fellow running back, longtime NFL linebacker Scott Shanle also expressed his disapproval. “Penalty f or being too physical and they will fine him too #crazy,” Shanle said on X. Fine forthcoming? Most definitely. First-time offenders are docked $23,882 for impermissible use of a helmet, with subsequent violations costing $47,762. Skattebo will have to cough up some cash this week. It will be interesting to see if this is something officials try to emphasize with the second-year pro down the road. Skattebo loves contact, and often looks to initiate it, usually by lowering head and shoulder. The Giants and Texans are tied at 14 late in the third quarter. Skattebo has gained 38 yards on 11 carries thus far. item.title: Kelce Returns Full-Go After Ankle Hit And No Fine From NFL
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The league chose not to punish the player who caused the hit, but that does not change the fact that Kelce is back on the field. It is a relief for fans who watched him leave early last Sunday. The Hit That Went Unpunished Chiefs fans saw the play early in the contest against the Los Angeles Chargers on October 18. Daiyan Henley wrapped up Kelce in a way that looked dangerous. Writing on X, PJ Green of the Kansas City Star stated that Daiyan Henley’s tackle on Travis Kelce involved a sliding hip drop with his shoulder striking Kelce’s ankle. The NFL Office of Gameday Accountability reviewed the play and decided not to fine Henley for on-field misconduct during Week 6. They did fine rookie guard Alex Harkey $5,277 for a late hit in the fourth quarter of that same game, but the man who hurt Kelce walked away with no penalty. Team doctors taped up Kelce’s ankle underneath and outside of his cleat last Sunday so he could return to action. He finished that game with four catches for 53 yards while playing through the pain. According to MARCA , Kelce was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Nevertheless, the official team report showed no injury designation when he entered the weekend. A Tough Test Awaits In Seattle The matchup against the Seattle Seahawks will take place at Lumen Field on Sunday, October 25. The game starts at 8:20 p.m. ET. This is the first real test for the Chiefs since they moved to a 5-0 record after beating the Chargers 22-6.

item.title: Lyon midfielder Pavel Šulc to be sidelined for four months with a meniscus injury
item.description: Lyon midfielder Pavel Šulc to be sidelined for four months with a meniscus injury Olympique Lyonnais’ Pavel Šulc (25) has suffered a meniscus injury to his right knee, the Rhône-based club confirmed on Sunday. Having picked up the injury during a training session ahead of OL’s away match against TSG Hoffenheim in the Europa League (3-0) last Thursday, the Czech midfielder is set to undergo surgery and “is expected to be sidelined for around four months” , according to the medical statement. Having been sidelined since the start of the season, Šulc will therefore be out of action until the end of February, or even early March 2027. This is a major blow for Les Gones, who will also have to do without Loïs Openda (26) – who suffered a fractured fibula against RC Lens (2-1) in early October – for several more weeks. Having made 10 appearances (five as a starter) for Lyon since the start of the season, Šulc has proved decisive on five occasions across all competitions, scoring two goals and providing three assists. GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Aaron Rodgers Passes Peyton Manning on NFL’s All Time Touchdown List
item.description: Photo by: Kirby Lee Steelers Quarterback Makes History in Victory Over Saints Aaron Rodgers added another historic achievement to his legendary NFL career on Sunday, passing Peyton Manning for sole possession of third place on the league’s all-time regular-season passing touchdown list. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback reached the milestone during the team’s 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. Rodgers connected with tight end Darnell Washington for a four-yard touchdown in the second quarter, recording the 540th regular season touchdown pass of his career and moving past Manning’s 539. The accomplishment came during a memorable international game, giving Rodgers another milestone to celebrate as he continues what he has announced will be his final NFL season. Rodgers Continues to Build His Hall of Fame Legacy Rodgers has spent more than two decades establishing himself as one of the greatest quarterbacks in football history. After beginning his career with the Green Bay Packers, where he spent 18 seasons, Rodgers played for the New York Jets before joining Pittsburgh. His career has included four NFL Most Valuable Player awards, a Super Bowl championship and countless memorable performances. Now, passing Manning on the touchdown list provides another accomplishment to add to an already impressive résumé. Manning finished his career with 539 regular season touchdown passes during his time with the Indianapolis Colts and Denver Broncos. Rodgers’ latest touchdown moves him into third place, putting him ahead of one of the most accomplished quarterbacks of Manning’s generation. Rodgers’ longevity has been especially impressive. Remaining productive long enough to pass a quarterback who retired more than a decade ago demonstrates how consistently he has produced throughout his career. Two Legends Remain Ahead of Rodgers Although Rodgers has passed Manning, two legendary quarterbacks remain ahead of him on the leaderboard. Drew Brees ranks second with 571 regular-season touchdown passes, while Tom Brady holds the NFL record with 649. Rodgers now needs 32 additional touchdown passes to match Brees and 110 to equal Brady’s mark. With Rodgers announcing that 2026 will be his final season, catching either quarterback would be an enormous challenge. Nevertheless, moving past Manning is a significant accomplishment regardless of what happens next. Rodgers has secured his place among the most productive passers the sport has ever seen. As Pittsburgh continues its push toward the postseason, Rodgers will look to build on Sunday’s victory and help the Steelers remain contenders. His historic touchdown against New Orleans provided another reminder that even late in his career, he can still make NFL history.

item.description: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent off
item.description: There are days when Tottenham go into these big games and find ways to beat themselves. This time, though, they held their nerve at a ground where they have mostly only known doom. Spurs played with control, stayed patient and won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018 after waiting for Chelsea to press the self-destruct button during a calamitous and comical ending to a cagey game. Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. Chelsea, short of poise on and off the pitch, deserved to be beaten at home for the first time this season and there was plenty of blame to go around after Alonso got his tactics wrong, Mike Penders scored a ridiculous own goal and Cole Palmer was sent off after a lunge on Conor Gallagher when he was already on a booking. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
